key_insight: A spatial AI biomarker that tracks whether high-risk morphology clusters are absent at the invasive tumor front can better stratify prognosis in early low- and intermediate-risk breast cancer than slide-level scoring alone.
clinical_relevance: In ER-positive/HER2-negative, node-negative grade 1–2 breast cancer, this marker may help identify patients with truly low recurrence risk as well as a hidden high-risk subgroup missed by global AI scores.
method: Vision-transformer tile scoring (ViT_DG) was applied to whole-slide images to detect high-grade morphology.
A binary biomarker was defined by the presence or absence of clustered high-risk tiles at the invasive tumor front.
Performance was tested in a Swedish multicenter cohort with a training set and an independent external validation set using multivariable Cox models.
evidence_signal: In 2,939 primary-subgroup patients across training and external test sets, tumor-front cluster absence was associated with better 10-year BCRFI and cluster-positive status showed about a 2.30-fold higher recurrence risk in the external test cohort.
watch_item: This is a retrospective pathology-AI study, so prospective validation and workflow standardization are needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer
